# OpenTelemetry slice telemetry log

**Status:** [DONE] — companion log for `plans/completed/opentelemetry-slice-telemetry.plans.md` (same workstream boundary; created per the tracker-handoff convention; archived with its tracker). Completed-step packets and compressed evidence summaries are archived here; the tracker keeps a compact [DONE] marker plus a reference to this file. This file is not gate-parsed — the tracker's fenced YAML packets remain the machine contract.

**Created by:** the `01-planning` mandate-patch pass that added the `## Mandates` section (`M-1`, `M-2`, `M-3`, `M-4`) and prepared **Step 08 — the session-logging and compression boundary** to the tracker. **The file was created EMPTY so the archive target exists before the first compression.** *(Historical record of the creation pass: at that moment nothing had been compressed into it — the compression of the tracker's existing history was the work of **Step 08**, not of the pass that created this file.)*

**First content — written by the `07-logging` STEP-08 COMPRESSION PASS. THE ARCHIVE IS NO LONGER EMPTY.** IT NOW HOLDS THE CLOSED SLICES' YAML PACKETS (`## Compressed steps`), THE FIX-PACKET BODY WITH ITS ANCHOR (`## Compressed fix packets`), THE EVIDENCE INDEX (`## Compressed evidence index`), THE FIVE PROSE PARAGRAPHS MOVED VERBATIM OUT OF THE TRACKER'S `## Latest validation evidence` (`## Compressed validation-evidence narrative`), AND THE RAW VALIDATION HISTORY (`## Compressed validation transcripts`).

**THE VERBATIM MOVES AND THE RECONSTRUCTED TRANSCRIPTS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF ARTEFACT, AND THE ARCHIVE SAYS WHICH IS WHICH.** THE PACKETS, THE FIX-PACKET BODY AND THE FIVE NARRATIVE PARAGRAPHS ARE **BYTE-VERBATIM MOVES**; THE TRANSCRIPT BODIES ARE **A RECONSTRUCTION** RECOVERED FROM THE PRE-COMPRESSION CORTEX RAG SNAPSHOT, CARRYING THEIR OWN REDACTIONS, THEIR GAP MARKERS AND THEIR PER-BLOCK WINDOW / RECOVERED-CHARACTER / GAP DESCRIPTOR TABLE. **THE PROVENANCE OF THAT SECTION IS STATED IN FULL AT ITS OWN HEADING AND IS THE AUTHORITATIVE DISCLOSURE — THIS HEADER IS A SUMMARY, NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR IT.** A TRACKER BLOCK DELETED BEFORE IT IS ARCHIVED LEAVES NO ORIGINAL BYTES TO MOVE, AND THE RAG SNAPSHOT IS THE ONLY SURVIVING COPY.

## How this log is used

- **THE COMPRESSION TARGET.** `07-logging` (Step 08) moves the closed slices' verbose detail, the fix-packet bodies, the repair transcripts and the raw validation history here at every slice close and every phase close, and replaces each with a short coverage note plus a reference to this file in the tracker. The tracker keeps the step header, the **full YAML packet of every open slice**, and the `fix-loop:` markers.
- **THE MACHINE-READABLE ARCHIVE — A PROSE-ONLY COMPRESSION IS A DEFECT.** A DONE slice that is compressed out of the tracker is rehydrated by `findArchivedSliceDescriptor` (`scripts/agent-customization/mcp/slice-context-archive.mjs`), which scans the **fenced YAML blocks of this file** for a `slices:` entry whose `slice_id` matches. **The moved YAML packet therefore keeps its `slices:` list** — if the archived copy is prose only, the slice stops resolving.
- **THE RAG TARGET.** The Cortex file filter is scoped to the plan family base name, so `search_context` matches this file as well as the tracker. Every archived fix packet keeps its **deterministic id** and its **HTML anchor comment** (`<!-- fix-packet-<slice_id>-iteration-<n> -->`) so the id resolves directly after the move.
- **THE LEDGER DESTINATION.** The terminal per-slice ledger block of a completed slice lives here, once the DONE writer lands. The transient dispatch record lives under `logs/slice-ledger/` and is deleted when the ledger block is written.
- **THE CLOSURE REVIEW LIVES ONCE, IN THE TRACKER.** The compact telemetry closure review (failures, unavailable data, anomalies, optimization — read from the existing ledgers only) is recorded one time in the tracker's `## Latest validation evidence` section at `plans/completed/opentelemetry-slice-telemetry.plans.md`. It is deliberately **not** duplicated here: this file remains the packet/ledger/transcript archive, and the review is a closure record, not a per-slice artefact.
- **THE PRIVACY BOUNDARY IS THE SAME HERE.** No exact start/end timestamp, no calendar date, no clock time, no wall-clock instant, no PII, no absolute user path, no git remote, no secret, no tool argument, no tool result, no file content and no prompt. Only durations and aggregate counters are persisted.

## Compressed steps

**STEP 01 — THE CONTRACT AND THE ATTRIBUTION EVIDENCE (PHASE 1).** TWO SLICES CLOSED AND WERE COMPRESSED OUT OF THE TRACKER BY THE `07-logging` STEP-08 PASS: `OT-S1-1` (THE RED CONTRACT HOME) AND `OT-S1-2` (THE CONTRACT DECLARATION MODULE). THE TRACKER KEEPS THE FULL YAML PACKET OF EVERY OPEN SLICE — `OT-S1-3`, `OT-S1-4` AND `OT-S1-5` — AND THE CLOSED SLICES' PACKETS ARE ARCHIVED BELOW **INTACT**, WITH THEIR `slices:` LIST, THEIR `files_to_change`, THEIR ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AND THEIR VALIDATION COMMANDS, SO `findArchivedSliceDescriptor` REHYDRATES THEM AND THE LIVE-TRACKER SCAN STILL SEES EACH CLOSED SLICE AS CLOSED. THE `fix-loop:` MARKER AND THE VERDICT TOKEN STAY IN THE TRACKER, ABOVE THE FIRST `###` OF ITS `## Latest validation evidence` SECTION.

**STEP 01 — THE SECOND COMPRESSION PASS (THE `07-logging` STEP-08 RE-ENTRANT LANE).** `OT-S1-4` — THE DISPATCH-TIME PRODUCER — CLOSED `[DONE]` ON THE REPAIRED BYTES AND WAS COMPRESSED OUT OF THE TRACKER BY THIS PASS. **THE PACKET BELOW IS ITS VERBATIM YAML, MOVED NOT PARAPHRASED**, SO `findArchivedSliceDescriptor` REHYDRATES `OT-S1-4` FROM THIS FILE EXACTLY AS IT REHYDRATES `OT-S1-1` AND `OT-S1-2`. THE `pre_execute_hook`, THE `auto_expand` FLAG, THE `constitution_check` AND THE PLAN-AMENDMENT COMMENT ARE **NOT** COPIED HERE ON PURPOSE: A LIVE DISPATCH BOUNDARY NEVER LIVES IN THIS FILE, AND THE LIVE STEP-01 PACKET IN THE TRACKER STAYS BOUND TO THE OPEN SLICE `OT-S1-5`. THE `validation` LIST BELOW IS **THE HISTORICAL VALIDATION SET OF `OT-S1-4`**, NOT THE LIVE ONE; THE LIVE STEP-01 VALIDATION LIST IN THE TRACKER NAMES `--slice-id=OT-S1-5`. **`OT-S1-3` IS STILL `[DONE]` AND ITS PACKET IS STILL LIVE IN THE TRACKER** — IT IS CARRIED FORWARD, NOT ARCHIVED, BECAUSE THE `step-packet` GATE ENFORCES A `green-only` FLOOR OF TWO SLICES ON A LIVE `[WIP]` STEP PACKET AND COMPRESSING `OT-S1-3` AS WELL WOULD LEAVE THE STEP WITH ONE SLICE AND FAIL THAT GATE; IT MOVES WHEN STEP 01 CLOSES.

**STEP 01 — THE CONTRACT AND THE ATTRIBUTION EVIDENCE (PHASE 1) — THE THIRD COMPRESSION PASS'S ARCHIVED COPY OF THE STEP PACKET.** THE `07-logging` STEP-08 RE-ENTRANT LANE (THE THIRD PASS OVER STEP 01) COMPRESSED THE LAST TWO SLICES OF THIS STEP OUT OF THE TRACKER — `OT-S1-3` (THE EXECUTABLE ATTRIBUTION PROBE) AND `OT-S1-5` (THE STEP-01 GREEN LANE) — AND BOTH ARE `[DONE]`. **THE PACKET BELOW IS THE TRACKER'S OWN STEP-01 PACKET WITH ITS `slices:` LIST INTACT, SO `findArchivedSliceDescriptor` REHYDRATES THE CLOSED SLICES FROM THIS FILE ALONE.** THE `slices:` LIST BELOW CARRIES THE TWO SLICES THIS PASS COMPRESSED OUT (`OT-S1-3` AND `OT-S1-5`); THE OTHER THREE CLOSED SLICES OF THIS STEP (`OT-S1-1`, `OT-S1-2` AND `OT-S1-4`) ARE IN THE FIRST-PASS ARCHIVED BLOCK ABOVE, WHICH IS WHY EVERY CLOSED SLICE OF THIS STEP STILL REHYDRATES FROM THIS FILE ALONE. **THE `pre_execute_hook`, THE `auto_expand` FLAG, THE `constitution_check` AND THE PLAN-AMENDMENT COMMENT ARE OMITTED ON PURPOSE: A LIVE DISPATCH BOUNDARY NEVER LIVES IN THIS FILE, AND THE STEP-01 DISPATCH BOUNDARY IS NOW STEP 02's (`OT-S1-6`).** **THE `phase_status` AND `phase_title` FIELDS ARE ADDED TO THIS ARCHIVED COPY ON PURPOSE, AND THEY ARE THE ONLY TWO FIELDS IN IT THAT ARE NOT A VERBATIM COPY OF THE TRACKER'S OWN STEP PACKET: THE ARCHIVE MODULE FALLS BACK TO `phase_status: DONE` WHEN A PACKET OMITS THE FIELD, AND PHASE 1 IS `[WIP]`, NOT DONE — STEP 02 IS STILL OPEN — SO THE FALLBACK WOULD STATE A FALSE PHASE STATE TO EVERY LANE THAT REHYDRATES THESE TWO SLICES. BOTH EARLIER ARCHIVED BLOCKS IN THIS SECTION CARRY `phase_status` FOR THE SAME REASON, AND THIS BLOCK NOW MATCHES THEM. BOTH VALUES ARE VERBATIM FROM THE TRACKER'S OWN PHASE-1 PACKET — `status: '[WIP]'` AND THE PHASE TITLE — SO ONLY THE KEY NAMES DIFFER, BECAUSE A STEP PACKET CARRIES NEITHER; AND THE LIVE DESCRIPTOR REPORTS THE SAME PHASE AS `WIP` (THE LIVE PATH REPORTS THE PHASE STATUS WITHOUT THE BRACKETS), SO BOTH FORMS STATE THE SAME PHASE STATE AND NEITHER SAYS DONE.**

**THE TWO `OT-S1-4` FIX PACKETS MOVED HERE VERBATIM, WITH THEIR ANCHORS.** THE ANCHOR COMMENTS ARE PRESERVED EXACTLY, **BUT A CORTEX RAG QUERY FOR EITHER PACKET ID DOES NOT RELIABLY RESOLVE THE ARCHIVED BODY** — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: THE CORPUS TOKENIZER REWRITES THE ID `fix-packet-OT-S1-4-iteration-2` INTO `fix* OR packet* OR OT OR S1 OR 4* OR iteration* OR 2*`, SO THE ANCHOR NEVER RANKED FIRST AND AN UNRELATED `fix-packet-P1-S2-4-iteration-1` CHUNK FROM ANOTHER PLAN OUTRANKED IT. **THE RELIABLE RETRIEVAL PATH IS THE PLAN-SCOPED `get_slice_context` WITH `plan_path` PINNED TO THIS PLAN** — IT REACHES THE ARCHIVED COPY (THE `OT-S1-5` CALL RETURNS `OT-S1-4` CHUNKS SOURCED FROM THIS FILE) — AND **AN UNPINNED CALL CAN RESOLVE A DIFFERENT PLAN AND ANSWER `notFound` ABOUT A SLICE THAT EXISTS**. BOTH PACKETS ARE **CLOSED**: ITERATION 1 CLOSED ON THE ROUND-2 `APPROVE` AND ITERATION 2 CLOSED ON THE `OT-S1-4` GREEN LANE, AND BOTH `fix-loop:` MARKERS READ `status=passed` IN THE TRACKER. THE TWO BODIES BELOW ARE **BYTE-VERBATIM MOVES** OF THE TRACKER'S OWN BLOCKS — NOTHING IS SUMMARISED, PARAPHRASED OR RECONSTRUCTED — SO A LANE THAT NEEDS THE FULL OBSERVATION, THE FULL REQUESTED-CHANGE LIST OR THE FULL NON-FIX LIST READS IT HERE EXACTLY AS IT READ IT IN THE TRACKER.

**THE ONE INTENTIONAL DEVIATION FROM VERBATIM, DISCLOSED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE.** THE TWO `OT-S1-4` FIX-PACKET BODIES BELOW ARE RE-INDENTED RELATIVE TO THE TRACKER'S OWN COPY, AND **THE RE-INDENT IS INDENTATION ONLY**: **28** NESTED CONTINUATION LINES PER BLOCK WERE SHIFTED **+2 SPACES**, AND THE CHARACTER CONTENT OF EVERY LINE IS IDENTICAL (**`contentDriftLines` IS EMPTY FOR BOTH BLOCKS**). **THE REASON IS THAT THE TRACKER'S OWN COPY OF BOTH PACKETS WAS NOT PARSEABLE YAML** — `js-yaml` REJECTS IT WITH `bad indentation of a mapping entry at line 25, column 5` (ITERATION 1) AND `bad indentation of a mapping entry at line 29, column 5` (ITERATION 2), BECAUSE THE `observations:` CONTINUATION KEYS SIT AT THE SAME INDENT AS THE `- source:` LIST ITEMS THEY CONTINUE — **SO THE ARCHIVED COPY, WHICH MUST PARSE FOR THE `## Recoverable packet index` AND THE REHYDRATION CONTRACT, IS THE PARSEABLE FORM.** **NO WORD, NO KEY, NO VALUE, NO OBSERVATION, NO REQUESTED CHANGE AND NO NON-FIX ENTRY WAS ADDED, REMOVED, REWORDED, REORDERED OR RE-INDENTED BEYOND THAT SHIFT**, AND THE TRACKER'S OWN SPELLING IS REPRODUCED EXACTLY WHERE IT APPEARED — **INCLUDING THE `OWINS`/`OWNS` ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE TRACKER'S TWO `OT-S1-4` GREEN RECORDS — **THE GREEN VALIDATION TRANSCRIPT (LOG BLOCK `### 21.`) SAYS `OWINS ITS MOVE`, WHILE THE GREEN LANE `PlanUpdate` SAYS `OWNS THE MOVE` IN BOTH ITS COMPANION-LOG FORM (LOG BLOCK `### 17.`) AND THE TRACKER'S OWN VERBATIM COPY (LOG BLOCK `### 23.`)** — WHICH IS NOT NORMALISED HERE. (MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED: THE THREE OCCURRENCES SIT AT LOG LINES 1541, 1906 AND 2117; THE ITERATION-2 LANE RECORDS `### 16.`/`### 22.` CARRY NO MOVE PHRASE AT ALL.)** EVERY OTHER MOVED REGION IN THIS COMPRESSION IS BYTE-VERBATIM.

### The `fix-packet-OT-S1-4-iteration-1` packet (the open iteration)

### The `fix-packet-OT-S1-4-iteration-2` packet (the open iteration)

**THE PACKET BELOW IS THE OPEN FIX PACKET OF `OT-S1-4` AND IT IS THE SCOPE OF THE NEXT DISPATCH (`04-implementing` FOR THIS PACKET). IT IS LOADED THROUGH CORTEX RAG BY ITS ID `fix-packet-OT-S1-4-iteration-2`, AND IT IS CLOSED ONLY BY A FRESH TIER-3 REVIEWER THAT RETURNS `APPROVE`.** IT CARRIES **THE SIX COVERAGE OBSERVATIONS (1-6)** OF THE `OT-S1-4` GREEN ROUND, WHICH RETURNED **NOT GREEN**: THE `code-coverage` GATE FAILS WHEN IT IS MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED FILE. **THIS PASS IS A PLANNING PASS: IT WRITES THE PACKET AND IT IMPLEMENTS NOTHING — NO SOURCE FILE, NO TEST FILE, NO COMMIT, NO BRANCH AND NO PULL REQUEST IS PART OF IT.** THE PACKET IS A COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS REPAIR, NOT A CONTRACT REPAIR: THE DISPATCH-RECORD CONTRACT, THE EIGHT-KEY USAGE BLOCK, THE NEVER-ZERO RULE, THE MACHINE-STABLE REASON TOKENS AND THE FAIL-OPEN WRITE ALL STAY EXACTLY AS THE ITERATION-1 REVIEW APPROVED THEM.

**THE THREE OBSERVATIONS THAT ARE **NOT** IN THIS PACKET, AND WHY.** OBSERVATION **7** (THE LONG-LIVED MCP SERVER PREDATING THE PRODUCER CHANGE) IS **THE `M-2` CLI/MCP RESET, A SCHEDULED PAUSE, NOT A FIX AND NOT AN ITERATION** — IT IS RECORDED IN THE `## Latest validation evidence` BLOCK BELOW AS PENDING AND IT IS CARRIED IN THIS PACKET AS AN EXPLICIT NON-FIX, SO THE IMPLEMENTING LANE CANNOT "FIX" IT. OBSERVATIONS **8** AND **9** (THE STALE STEP-01 VALIDATION LIST AND THE STALE `AC-011-A` SESSION-KEY TEXT) ARE **RESOLVED BY THE `01-planning` LANE THAT WROTE THIS PACKET** — SEE THE `## PlanUpdate` BLOCK AT THE END OF THIS TRACKER. **OBSERVATIONS 5 AND 6 ARE HALF-IN-PACKET AND HALF-ROUTED: THE ARTEFACT HYGIENE IS A RE-MEASUREMENT PROCEDURE FOR THE IMPLEMENTING LANE, AND THE MERGE SEMANTICS AND THE BASELINE POLICY BEHIND THEM ARE `00-helping`'s — THE PACKET FORBIDS THE IMPLEMENTING LANE FROM EDITING ANY TRACKED FILE OUTSIDE THE TWO-FILE WRITE SET TO WORK AROUND THEM.**

The home resolves the contract module **lazily inside every `it()`**, so an unimplemented contract is an **assertion failure that names the missing contract** — never an import failure, never a collection error, never a skipped file. **Fixture and cleanup notes:**

- **The activation set is FROZEN, not re-measured at run time.** The home carries a literal, sorted list of the **536** slice ids the live trackers already record as DONE, measured at RED time by the lane and cross-checked against the live trackers by an in-lane assertion (`every frozen id is STILL DONE in the live trackers`), so the exemption is provable against the live trackers and not invented. Re-measuring it on every run would silently turn R-7 into "every slice that happens to be DONE right now is exempt", which is wrong the moment a post-activation slice completes — that is the exact trap the forward-only rule exists to close.

**TWO LIVE-PATH DEFECTS FOUND BY THE COVERAGE TIER-3 REVIEW (not fixed by this lane — this lane edits no production byte):**

- **D-2 (LOW, silent value loss)** — `isPlainObject` (`:327`) is `typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)`, so a `Date`, a `Map` or a class instance passes as a plain object and `emitLedgerBlock` renders it as an **empty mapping** — the value is **silently lost** instead of emitted as `null`. Only `symbol`/`function` reach the `null` fallback (`:317`). Fix: restrict `isPlainObject` to a real plain object (prototype is `Object.prototype` or `null`) and let exotic values take the `null` path.

Neither defect violates `AC-003-B` as written (the scanner does return the exact offending key; the emitter stays byte-identical for identical inputs), so neither is a slice-level gate failure — but **both live in a file no later slice owns**, so they should be closed while `OT-S1-2` is still the owner.

### The RED home — what it pins (`scripts/telemetry/probe-attribution-sources.test.mjs`, 16 lanes)

| describe block | lane | what it pins |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **the five ratified obligations** | the host hook event and its payload fields are named with a resolving `file:line` | the plan''s obligation (a) — the host post-tool event and the payload field the probe relies on |
| | the absence of a documented session-id env var is named with a resolving `file:line` | obligation (b) — the repo-invented fallbacks are the evidence |
| | the `token_count` computation site is named, together with its ABSENCE of persistence | obligation (c) — computed at runtime, never stored |
| | the absence of a per-slice LLM token source is named | obligation (d) — the declared-but-never-measured fields |
| | the write-tool hook exists and its exact limits are named | obligation (e) — the hook surface is evidence that the repo receives the host payload, NOT the counter |
| **the citation integrity** | every signal names a repo-relative `file:line` that RESOLVES to a real file and a real line | AC-005-B, first half |
| | every signal cites a line that actually SUPPORTS the signal it claims | the anti-decoration rule — see below |
| | the probe holds NO hardcoded `file:line` literal | the probe must INSPECT the live repository, not recite a memorised list |
| | the duration signal agrees with the live elapsed-measurement site | the duration verdict is an ORACLE, not an assertion |
| | the delivered-context-token signal agrees with the live `token_count` site | the same, for the token signal |
| **the research-artifact agreement** | the research artifact names every signal | AC-005-B, second half |
| | the research artifact agrees with the probe report on every demonstrated signal | the artifact may not drift from the probe |
| | any machine-readable report embedded in the research artifact agrees with the probe report | the artifact may not carry a second, contradictory report |
| **the dependent gating** | the report carries a per-signal verdict a dependent slice can read | AC-013-A |

### The anti-decoration rule (the heart of the contract)

A citation that merely RESOLVES is not evidence. The home requires that the cited line — or a line within two of it — is **ABOUT** the signal it claims, and it adds three rules:

1. a citation into **`plans/`** never counts — the tracker and the research artifact DESCRIBE the sources, they are not sources, so citing them is circular;
2. a citation into a **TEST file** never counts — a test is not a source;
3. a signal claimed as **`demonstrated`** may not cite a **bare quoted field name** — a schema field that DECLARES `prompt_tokens` is not a source that MEASURES them, and the same reasoning disqualifies a `duration_ms` schema entry as a duration source. A signal claimed as **`unavailable`** MAY cite a declaration, because naming the declared-but-never-measured field is exactly how an absence is evidenced.

RANGE citations (`file:START-END`) are parsed, resolved and windowed, so a probe may cite a block; a range whose EVERY line is a bare quoted field name still counts as a bare declaration.

### The live oracles the home computes INDEPENDENTLY of the probe

The home does not take the probe''s word for the two verdicts the tracker ratifies as MEASURED. It recomputes them from the live repository:

- **the duration signal** — the home scans `src/` for a file that READS a monotonic clock (`performance.now`, `resolveHighResolutionNow`) AND carries an elapsed notion, excluding test files; the verdict must be `demonstrated` iff such a site exists;
- **the delivered-context-token signal** — the home scans the MCP surface and `rag-index/` for a `token_count` computation site, excluding test files; the verdict must be `demonstrated` iff such a site exists;
- **the tool-execution signal** — the home scans `.github/hooks/*.json` for a `PostToolUse` (or `PostToolUseFailure`) key and requires the citation to sit under the host hook surface;
- **the LLM signal** — the verdict must be `unavailable` with a reason, because the tracker measures that there is NO per-slice LLM token-consumption source in this repository today.

### The fixture and cleanup contract

- **fixture type** — a MINIMAL, DETERMINISTIC, SELF-INSPECTING STUB PROBE plus a generated research artifact. There is NO mock, NO fixture file and NO network in the shipped home.
- **determinism** — the stub probe INSPECTS the live repository at runtime and builds every citation BY CONCATENATION, so it holds no literal `file:line` string (the shipped anti-hardcoding regex matches NONE of the nine variant sources). The home pins NO seed and NO fixed timestamp.
- **cleanup** — the stub probe and its artifact live entirely under the gitignored `tmp/` tree; the shipped home creates NOTHING, so it leaves no state behind. The probe run is memoized per test file, so it is invoked at most once per suite.
- **isolation** — the probe is executed as a CHILD PROCESS (`execFileSync(process.execPath, [PROBE_PATH], { cwd: REPO_ROOT })`), so a probe that calls `process.exit` on import cannot kill the Jest worker, and a probe whose stdout is not a single JSON document fails the test rather than hanging it.

## The OT-V2-2 implementing lane — the Vertical B implementation record (04-implementing, Tier 1)

### 39. PlanUpdate — THE `OT-V2-2` IMPLEMENTING LANE (04-implementing, Tier 1)

**WHAT LANDED, SEAM BY SEAM.** SIX OF THE SIX DECLARED `files_to_change` SEAMS ARE ON DISK, AND ONE MORE SEAM LANDED OUTSIDE THE DECLARED SET AND IS DISCLOSED BELOW. THE SIX DECLARED SEAMS ARE: THE FAIL-OPEN OBSERVER `scripts/agent-customization/hooks/slice-usage-hook.mjs`; THE TRACKED MANIFEST EDIT `.github/hooks/cortex-refresh.json`; THE FAIL-CLOSED DONE GATE `scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-ledger.gate.mjs`; THE THIN SWEEP WRAPPER `scripts/telemetry/privacy-sweep.mjs`; THE IDEMPOTENT LOCAL ENABLEMENT `scripts/telemetry/ensure-local-telemetry.mjs`; AND THE FIVE-STATE CLASSIFIER `scripts/telemetry/ledger-state.mjs`. THE SEVENTH, DISCLOSED, SEAM IS THE DONE WRITER `scripts/telemetry/write-slice-ledger.mjs`, WHICH CARRIES BOTH THE USER-REQUESTED IDEMPOTENT-WRITE LEDGER CLEANUP AND THE CRLF FIX DESCRIBED LATER IN THIS BLOCK.

**THE OBSERVER (`scripts/agent-customization/hooks/slice-usage-hook.mjs`).** IT IS FAIL-OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION: A FAILED OBSERVATION NEVER FAILS THE TOOL CALL IT OBSERVED, AND IT WRITES NOTHING WHEN NO DISPATCH RECORD IS OPEN. EVERY OBSERVATION APPENDS EXACTLY ONE LINE AND EVERY LINE CARRIES EXACTLY FIVE FIELDS — `seq`, `slice_id`, `session_key`, `bucket` AND `outcome` — AND CARRIES NO TOOL NAME, NO ARGUMENT, NO RESULT, NO ERROR CONTENT, NO CONTENT, NO PATH, NO INSTANT, NO CALENDAR DATE AND NO RAW SESSION ID. THE `seq` IS THE APPEND-TIME LINE INDEX, NOT A RANDOM OR A CLOCK, AND THE DONE WRITER COUNTS LINES RATHER THAN DISTINCT `seq` VALUES, SO A CONCURRENT APPEND CANNOT INFLATE THE COUNTER. THE TWO COMPLETION OUTCOMES ARE COUNTED AND NAMED SEPARATELY, AND THE COUNTERS ARE THE FIVE SAFE BUCKETS, NEVER AN ARGUMENT LIST.

**THE REGISTRATION (`.github/hooks/cortex-refresh.json`).** TWO OBSERVER ENTRIES WERE ADDED BESIDE THE EXISTING WRITE-REINDEX HOOK — ONE UNDER THE SUCCESS EVENT KEY AND ONE UNDER THE FAILURE EVENT KEY — BOTH RUNNING THE SAME COMMAND AND BOTH CARRYING **NO** MATCHER FIELD, SO AN INVALID PATTERN CAN NEVER SILENTLY SKIP THE OBSERVER AND A FAILING TOOL CALL IS NEVER MISSED. THE LOCAL ENABLEMENT COMMAND REPORTS THE TRACKED MANIFEST AND NEVER REWRITES IT AT RUNTIME.

**THE DONE GATE (`scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-ledger.gate.mjs`).** IT IS FAIL-CLOSED AND IT SCANS THE TRACKER FOR THE SLICES MARKED DONE AT OR AFTER THE ACTIVATION MARKER, AND IT REQUIRES EXACTLY ONE VALID LEDGER BLOCK PER SUCH SLICE. THE FAILURE KINDS ARE `missing-ledger`, `duplicate-ledger`, `invalid-ledger` AND `unattributable-ledger`. A MISSING, MALFORMED, DUPLICATED, SCHEMA-UNKNOWN OR FORBIDDEN-FIELD LEDGER IS A HARD FAILURE; A COUNTER THAT CLAIMS AVAILABILITY WITHOUT A SOURCE, A MEASURES STRING AND A SCOPE IS REFUSED; AN UNAVAILABLE COUNTER WRITTEN AS ZERO IS REFUSED; AND THE LAYER-A REPORTING STATES ARE NEVER AN EXEMPTION FROM THE LEDGER, SO ONLY THE LAYER-B CORRUPT STATE BLOCKS THE TRANSITION. THE PRE-EXISTING DONE SLICES ARE OUT OF SCOPE AND ARE NEVER BACK-FILLED, AND THE GATE NEVER DEMANDS A BACKFILL. THE REPORT IS ONE COMPACT JSON LINE ON STDOUT AND THE REFUSAL PROSE GOES TO STDERR.

**THE SWEEP (`scripts/telemetry/privacy-sweep.mjs`).** IT IS A THIN WRAPPER OVER THE ONE FORBIDDEN-KEY AND FORBIDDEN-VALUE SCANNER EXPORTED BY `scripts/telemetry/telemetry-contract.mjs` AND IT INTRODUCES NO SECOND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE RULES. IT COVERS THE SIX PERSISTED ARTEFACTS WITH NO EXCLUSION — THE LAYER-A JSONL, THE TOOL-EXECUTION OBSERVATION LOG, THE COMPANION LOG, THE COMPACT PLAN MIRROR, THE EXTRACTION CURSOR AND THE DERIVED SIDECAR INDEX — IT ALWAYS REPORTS AN EMPTY EXCLUSION LIST, AND IT EXITS NON-ZERO ON ANY VIOLATION.

**THE LOCAL ENABLEMENT (`scripts/telemetry/ensure-local-telemetry.mjs`).** IT IS IDEMPOTENT, IT CREATES THE LOCAL SETTINGS UNDER THE LOCAL TELEMETRY FOLDER WITH TRACES, METRICS AND LOGS ALL ENABLED AND THE LOCAL JSONL SINK, IT UPGRADES A STALE SCHEMA VERSION, IT QUARANTINES A CORRUPT FILE TO A `.bak` SIBLING, IT PRINTS THE EXACT CHANGED PATHS AND THE EXACT REMEDIATION FOR THE TRACKED HOOK REGISTRATION, AND IT NEVER CONTACTS THE NETWORK.

**THE CLASSIFIER (`scripts/telemetry/ledger-state.mjs`).** IT RETURNS EXACTLY ONE OF ENABLED, DISABLED, STALE, CORRUPT OR NO-DATA WITH THE ARTEFACT THAT PRODUCED THE VERDICT AND THE REASON, IT PERFORMS NO RECOVERY OF ITS OWN, AND IT REPORTS A RECOVERED LEDGER HONESTLY AS `measurement_state` UNAVAILABLE — NEVER AS MEASURED, NEVER WITH A ZERO DURATION AND NEVER WITH A ZERO COUNTER.

**THE FOCUSED LANES THIS LANE ADDED — EIGHT OF THEM, IN THE OWNER-LOCAL HOMES, WITH NO NEW TEST FILE.** THE WRITER HOME GAINED THE LANE THAT PROVES THE TRANSIENT DISPATCH RECORD IS REMOVED ON AN IDEMPOTENT WRITE TOO, AND THE LANE THAT FINDS AN EXISTING BLOCK IN A CRLF COMPANION LOG AND WRITES NO SECOND BLOCK. THE OBSERVER HOME GAINED THE LANE THAT CONTINUES THE `seq` FROM A PRE-SEEDED OBSERVATION LOG. THE GATE HOME GAINED THE LANE THAT NEVER REWRITES THE COMPANION LOG IT READS, THE LANE THAT REPORTS THE PRE-EXISTING DONE SET IT EXEMPTED, AND THE LANE THAT READS A CRLF TRACKER AND REFUSES A DONE SLICE WITH NO LEDGER. THE ENABLEMENT HOME GAINED THE LANE THAT FALLS BACK TO THE DEFAULT ARTEFACT SET OF THE LANE WHEN NO TARGET IS NAMED.

## The Step-11 hygiene pass — the pointer-stack retirement and the ledger-block correction

**THIS SECTION CLOSES THE `07-logging` STEP-11 HYGIENE PASS AGAINST THE TRACKER's OWN BYTES. IT RECORDS TWO THINGS: THE RETIREMENT OF THE REMAINING DISPATCH-POINTER STACK FROM THE TRACKER, AND THE CORRECTION OF A FALSE STATEMENT THE SAME PASS HAD WRITTEN ABOUT THE LEDGER BLOCKS. NOTHING ABOVE IS REWRITTEN — THIS FILE IS APPEND-ONLY, AND EVERY SUPERSEDED COUNT AND EVERY SUPERSEDED CLAIM STAYS WHERE IT IS.**

**THE RETIREMENT OF THE POINTER STACK — MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED.** THE TRACKER's `## The retired dispatch-pointer stack (superseded — appendix)` SECTION NOW HOLDS **ONE** PARAGRAPH — THE ARCHIVE NOTICE — AND **NOT ONE** OF THE TWENTY-ONE HISTORICAL DISPATCH POINTERS IS STILL IN THE TRACKER. THE PARAGRAPHS THAT THE EARLIER PASS HAD LEFT BEHIND WERE REMOVED IN THIS PASS BY BYTE-VERBATIM MOVE AND WITHOUT RE-TRANSCRIPTION: THE `OT-S1-4` ITERATION-2 `04-implementing` LANE, THE `M-2` RESET PARAGRAPH, THE `OT-S1-4` ITERATION-2 ITERATION MARKER, THE `01-planning` TRACKER-PATCH LANE, THE "NOW READS" AND "PENDING" PARAGRAPHS, THE "TWO OBSERVATIONS" AND "THIS LANE IMPLEMENTED NOTHING" PARAGRAPHS, THE `OT-S1-3` FIX-PACKET-ITERATION-1 LANE, THE SUPERSEDED ELEVENTH, TENTH, NINTH, EIGHTH, SEVENTH, SIXTH AND FIFTH LANES, THE SUPERSEDED REPAIR TRANCHE, THE SUPERSEDED REPAIR LANE AND THE SUPERSEDED SECOND LANE. **EVERY ONE OF THEM ALREADY STOOD VERBATIM IN THE `## The retired dispatch-pointer stack — the archived chain` SECTION ABOVE, AND THE FIVE WHOSE FIRST COPY HERE WAS CONDENSED RATHER THAN BYTE-VERBATIM STAND VERBATIM IN THE `## The retired dispatch-pointer stack — the verbatim correction block` SECTION ABOVE.** THE TRACKER NOW CARRIES EXACTLY **ONE** AUTHORITATIVE DISPATCH POINTER — THE ONE UNDER `## Handoff query` — AND THE STRAY `THE COMPANION LOG IS THE ARCHIVE.` LINE AND THE ACCUMULATED BLANK RUN BESIDE THE APPENDIX WERE REMOVED WITH IT.

**THE CORRECTION — A FALSE STATEMENT THIS PASS HAD WRITTEN.** THE TRACKER's STEP-11 REOPENING RECORD AND THE STEP-11 PACKET's `next_step` HAD SAID THAT **THE TWO TERMINAL `telemetry_ledger:` BLOCKS FOR `OT-V2-2` AND `OT-V2-3` DO NOT EXIST** AND THAT **THE DONE GATE STILL READS VACUOUSLY (NO IN-SCOPE `[DONE]` SLICE, ZERO CHECKED LEDGERS)**, AND THE TRACKER's LIVE HANDOFF BODY HAD SAID THAT **THE COMPANION LOG HOLDS TWO REAL `telemetry_ledger:` BLOCKS** AND HAD NAMED **`03-red-testing` FOR `OT-V2-1`** AS THE NEXT LANE. **ALL OF THOSE STATEMENTS WERE WRONG, AND THEY WERE WRONG IN THE SAME WAY: THEY WERE CARRIED FROM THE STOPPED BROAD LANE'S FROZEN EVIDENCE BLOCK, WHICH IS A HISTORICAL READING AND NOT THE LIVE ONE.** THE CORRECTED FACT, MEASURED AGAINST THIS FILE'S OWN BYTES, IS: **THIS FILE HOLDS SIX CANONICAL `telemetry_ledger:` BLOCKS — `OT-V1-2`, `OT-V1-3`, `OT-V2-1`, `OT-V2-4`, `OT-V2-2` AND `OT-V2-3`** — WHICH IS WHAT THE `## The ledger-block census — the current, authoritative count` SECTION ABOVE ALREADY STATES; `OT-V2-2` AND `OT-V2-3` BOTH CARRY `status: '[DONE]'`; THE SLICES `OT-V2-2`, `OT-V2-3` AND `OT-V2-4` ARE ALL `[DONE]` IN THE TRACKER AND EACH CARRIES A LEDGER BLOCK, SO THE DONE GATE's IN-SCOPE SET IS **NOT EMPTY**; `OT-V2-3` CARRIES 1107 OBSERVED EXECUTIONS — 1082 COMPLETED, 25 FAILED — OVER 10 SESSIONS, `OT-V2-4` CARRIES 28 — 26 COMPLETED, 2 FAILED — OVER 4 SESSIONS, AND `OT-V2-2` IS HONESTLY UNAVAILABLE WITH `unavailable_reason: 'no_observations_for_slice'` AND EVERY NUMERIC `null`, NEVER `0`; AND THE WRITER's HARD-CODED `observer_not_loaded` REASON HAS BEEN REPLACED BY `REASON_NO_OBSERVATIONS_FOR_SLICE` IN `scripts/telemetry/write-slice-ledger.mjs`, SO THE **MEASURED COUNTER IS LANDED** AND IS NOT A REMAINING GAP.

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNMET, MEASURED AGAINST THE REPOSITORY.** (1) **THE PRUNER IS NOT WIRED** — `scripts/telemetry/prune-dispatch-records.mjs` EXISTS AND ITS OWN HOME IS GREEN, BUT IT IS A STANDALONE CLI: `scripts/telemetry/write-slice-ledger.mjs` NEVER IMPORTS `pruneDispatchRecords` AND NEVER CALLS IT, SO NO RUNTIME PATH PRUNES A DISPATCH RECORD AND A DISPATCH RECORD OF A SLICE THAT NEVER REACHED A LEDGER WRITE SURVIVES FOREVER. (2) **THE INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PASS HAS RECORDED NO VERDICT ON THE RE-SCOPED BYTES** — THE FOUR PRIOR ROUNDS ALL RULED ON THE PRE-RE-SCOPE BYTES. (3) NEITHER STEP 11 NOR PHASE 8 IS FLIPPED. **THE MEASURED COUNTER IS NOT AMONG THEM.** THE TRACKER's STEP-11 REOPENING RECORD, ITS `next_step`, ITS PHASE-8 `next_phase`, ITS `## Handoff query` POINTER AND ITS LIVE HANDOFF BODY HAVE ALL BEEN CORRECTED TO THIS FACT, SO THE CORRECTION IS NOW STATED IN THE TRACKER ITSELF AND NOT ONLY HERE.

**THE TWO ARCHIVE REGIONS THAT REMAIN IN THE TRACKER ARE UNCHANGED AND STILL DEFERRED** — THE SUPERSEDED SIX-PHASE CHAIN AND THE CLOSED `fix-packet-OT-S1-6-iteration-1`..`4` EVIDENCE BODIES — AND THE PRECISE RESUME POINT IS THE `## The deferred archive work — the precise resume point` SECTION ABOVE. **NO IMPLEMENTATION BYTE WAS CHANGED BY THIS PASS, NO SUBAGENT WAS DISPATCHED, AND NO VERDICT WAS ISSUED, REISSUED OR RETRACTED.**

## The rules this file is held to

1. **THE TRACKER NEVER CARRIES A VERBOSE `[DONE]` RECORD, AND THIS FILE NEVER CARRIES A LIVE PACKET.** An open or dispatchable slice's YAML packet stays in the tracker; a closed slice's YAML packet is moved here intact, with its `slices:` list, its `files_to_change`, its acceptance criteria and its validation commands.
2. **THE `fix-loop:` MARKERS STAY IN THE TRACKER, ABOVE THE FIRST `###` OF ITS `## Latest validation evidence` SECTION.** The convergence tracker reads the tracker file only and truncates that section at the next heading of any level; a marker that leaves the tracker, or that falls below that truncation point, silently zeroes the iteration count and loses the escalation signal.
3. **THE FIX-PACKET ANCHORS SURVIVE THE MOVE VERBATIM.**
4. **NO SCRIPT EVER REWRITES A TRACKER OR THIS FILE.** The compact WIP telemetry mirror is written into the tracker by the `07-logging` lane as a tracker edit, and the terminal ledger block is written into this file by the DONE writer.
5. **THE PRIVACY SWEEP COVERS THIS FILE WITH NO EXCLUSION.**

## Scope

This tracker authors the execution plan for **per-slice telemetry in the NeatapticTS agent workflow**. It measures how long a slice took, how many tool **executions completed inside that slice's dispatch window**, and how many RAG-context tokens were **delivered** to it, and it records those numbers in a repo-owned, versioned, per-slice ledger. Two boundaries are load-bearing and are stated in full in *The token and tool-execution attribution contract*: the tool signal is a count of **completed executions, never a count of issued tool calls** (a call denied before execution does not complete and is not counted), and the token signal is **context tokens delivered, never model token consumption**.

The work is **two layers that are deliberately independent**, because they fail in opposite directions and neither may be allowed to mask the other:

| layer | owner | failure policy | persistence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A — the OpenTelemetry signal layer** | `src/observability/` (library boundary) + `scripts/telemetry/` (repo tooling) | **fail-open / warn-only** — a telemetry failure never fails a slice, never crashes a caller, never blocks a DONE transition | local-only sanitized JSONL under `logs/telemetry/` |
| **B — the repo-owned per-slice measurement and ledger** | the shared measurement-state module `scripts/telemetry/slice-usage.mjs`, the dispatch-time producer inside `scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-workflow-mcp.mjs`, the tool-execution observer `scripts/agent-customization/hooks/slice-usage-hook.mjs`, the DONE writer `scripts/telemetry/write-slice-ledger.mjs` and the DONE gate `scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-ledger.gate.mjs` | **fail-closed for NEW `[DONE]` transitions** — a slice that is marked `[DONE]` without a valid ledger is refused | one fenced YAML block per completed slice in the associated `.logs.md`; the **transient** dispatch record lives under `logs/slice-ledger/` and is **deleted** when the ledger block is written |

Layer B does **not** depend on layer A. Layer A being disabled, broken, unavailable or mis-configured **never** removes the obligation to write the ledger. This is the load-bearing rule of the whole design and it is pinned by `AC-001`, `AC-006`, `AC-007` and `AC-012`.

**The ownership rule the layer split enforces (this is what keeps the duration out of the fail-open layer).** Layer B **produces** every per-slice measurement — the slice begin/end instants, the monotonic duration, the usage deltas, the retry and interruption recovery and the transient-state cleanup. Layer A may **consume** the finished measurement (it may emit the snapshot as a span, a metric and a log), but layer A is **never required to produce it**, and no layer-A reporting state (`ENABLED`, `DISABLED`, `STALE`, `CORRUPT`, `NO-DATA`) can remove a layer-B obligation. The layer-A state and the layer-B measurement state are reported as **two independent fields** in the ledger (`otel_state` and `measurement_state`) and never collapse into one. Pinned by `AC-012`.

**Constitution authority.** `plans/constitution.md` is the authority for this tracker's guardrails, and every phase and step packet in this tracker carries a `constitution_check:` key naming the exact ids it exercises: `principle-1-ai-thinking-partner`, `principle-2-human-mission-ai-method`, `principle-3-verbatim-binding`, `principle-4-breadth-first-recoverable`, `principle-5-unique-ids`, `section-security-cross-platform`, `section-development-workflow` and `section-governance-versioning`. The principles this lane exercises directly are **Principle 2** (the human owns the mission and the AI owns the method inside the guardrails — the measured signals are evidence for the human's decision, never a substitute for it), **Principle 3** (the user-confirmed scope is bound verbatim: traces + metrics + logs, local-only JSONL, later automatic local enablement, a balanced OTel-fail-open / forward-only DONE-ledger-fail-closed split, a compact WIP mirror, Standard runtime metadata only, no timestamps/dates/clock times/PII in any persisted artifact, transient timing removed at completion, token usage + tool-call counts + duration as the highest-priority measures, unavailable counters as `null` + a reason and never a fake zero, no tool arguments or content, and no racer or acceleration-timing changes) and **Principle 4** (breadth-first and recoverable — the two layers fail in opposite directions, and every transient state has a defined recovery path).

### Non-goals (explicit, binding)

- **No** auto-instrumentation (`auto-instrumentations-node`, `instrumentation-*` packages) and **no** monkey-patching of `http`/`fs`/`net`.
- **No** logger replacement and **no** interception of the repo's existing console/`logger` output.
- **No** collector, **no** remote OTLP, **no** third-party egress, **no** network calls from the telemetry path.
- **No** source text, file contents, prompts, tool arguments, tool results, diffs, or any other payload in a persisted artifact.
- **No** secrets, **no** absolute user paths, **no** git remotes, **no** PII of any kind in a persisted artifact.
- **No** exact start/end timestamps, calendar dates, clock times or wall-clock instants in any persisted artifact. Only durations and aggregate counters are persisted.
- **No** platform / architecture / CPU-count / total-memory fingerprinting. The runtime metadata set is exactly: Node version, duration, validation results, heap usage, RSS usage.
- **No** `neat.acceleration.*` timing metrics (see `R-9`).
- **No** backfill of the 19 pre-existing `[DONE]` slices. That count is the one **stated in the user directive**; the implementation slice measures the exact per-tracker `[DONE]` set and records it as evidence, and the **measured** set is the authoritative one for the forward-only rule. The ledger is **forward-only**.
- **No** change to the NEAT-algorithm telemetry tree `src/neat/telemetry/` and **no** change to the public API barrel `src/neataptic.ts`.
- **No** change to the paused racer workstream (`plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`) or to any racer implementation file. Its tracker is read-only input for the extraction strategy only.
- **No** redefinition of the existing Chrome/Perfetto "trace" vocabulary (`scripts/analyze-trace/*`, `LONG_TASK_THRESHOLD_MS`). The OpenTelemetry "trace" signal is a distinct concept and this tracker uses the name `otel` in every metric, span and file name to keep the two apart.

## The two-layer architecture

### Layer A — the OpenTelemetry signal layer (fail-open)

**Scope:** OpenTelemetry JS **traces + metrics + logs, all three**.

**Export boundary:** a repo-local JSONL exporter per signal, implemented inside `src/observability/telemetry/`. No OTLP exporter package is installed and no collector is contacted. The exported records are the ONLY thing that reaches disk from this layer.

**Privacy design at the export boundary (the load-bearing part):** the normal OpenTelemetry record shape carries `startTime`, `endTime`, `timeUnixNano` and `observedTimestamp`. Those are **never** written. The exporter converts the interval into a single `duration_ms` derived from the span's monotonic duration and **drops the instants**. The sanitizer is an **allow-list**, not a deny-list: a field is written only if it is explicitly permitted for that signal, so an unknown or newly-added SDK attribute is dropped by default rather than leaked by default. A deny-list of forbidden key names and forbidden value patterns (ISO-8601 datetimes, calendar dates, epoch-millisecond literals, absolute Windows/POSIX user paths, e-mail addresses) runs as a **second, independent** pass so a bug in the allow-list still cannot leak a forbidden field.

**Durations** are measured with `performance.now()` (monotonic) — but the quantity measured **in this layer** is the **exported span's own interval** (the length of the OpenTelemetry record being written), **never the slice window**. The slice begin/end instants, the monotonic **slice** duration, the usage deltas, the retry and interruption recovery and the transient-state deletion are owned **exclusively** by the layer-B DONE path, and the layer-A session module never computes them (`AC-009-A`, `AC-012-D`). The repo's existing split-clock pattern (`src/neat/evolve/runtime/evolve.runtime.utils.ts:152-158` / `:211-218`, `resolveHighResolutionNow()` with a `Date.now()` fallback) and the injectable-clock precedent (`examples/neatRacing/ai/runtime.adaptation.ts:263,301,376,710`, `options.now ?? Date.now`) are the model for deterministic tests.

**Fail-open:** every exporter call is wrapped so that a rejected export, a missing optional peer dependency, a full disk or an unwritable sink produces a **warn-only** diagnostic and never an exception into the caller. The precedent is `src/neat/telemetry/runtime/telemetry.runtime.ts:73-93` (`safelyStreamTelemetryEntry()` swallows observer failures).

**Deterministic shutdown / flush per supported entry point:**

| entry point | flush / shutdown mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Node CLI (`scripts/telemetry/*.mjs`) | explicit `await shutdownTelemetry()` before the CLI returns; `SimpleSpanProcessor` and `SimpleLogRecordProcessor` export synchronously, `PeriodicExportingMetricReader.forceFlush()` is awaited |
| Jest | a single root-level `globalTeardown` (`scripts/telemetry/jest-telemetry-teardown.mjs`) flushes and shuts the layer down once per run |
| library / embedder | `startTelemetrySession()` / `shutdownTelemetry()` are exported from `src/observability/telemetry/`; the module is **side-effect free until started**, and a missing optional peer dependency degrades to a no-op |

### Layer B — the repo-owned per-slice YAML ledger (fail-closed)

**Canonical artifact:** one fenced `yaml` block per newly completed slice in the associated companion log (`plans/<plan>.logs.md`). The block is keyed by `plan_id` + `slice_id` and carries `schema_version: 1`.

**Ownership at the DONE transition:** the `07-logging` lane owns the transition. It calls the writer (`scripts/telemetry/write-slice-ledger.mjs`), which **upserts** the block for that `(plan_id, slice_id)` — a re-run replaces the block in place instead of appending a duplicate, so the ledger is **idempotent** and there is **exactly one ledger per newly completed slice**.

**Ownership of the measurement itself — the dispatch-time producer (the only component that knows the slice id).** The per-slice record is opened at **dispatch** time by the one repo-owned module that is handed the slice id: `get_slice_context` inside `scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-workflow-mcp.mjs` (the `pre_execute_hook` tool of every step packet). On every call it writes **one transient, timestamp-free dispatch record** under `logs/slice-ledger/dispatch/` carrying:

- `plan_id` and `slice_id` — the identity of the slice being dispatched;
- `context_tokens_delivered` — the `token_count` the MCP already computes for that slice (see `AC-011`);
- `dispatch_seq` — the number of tool-execution observations already recorded when the slice was dispatched (the **window start**);
- `started_monotonic_ns` — a **monotonic** nanosecond counter (`process.hrtime.bigint()`), never a wall-clock instant; it exists only in this transient record and is deleted with it.

The dispatch record is the **open-slice pointer**: the observer described below reads it and **stamps** each observed execution with the `slice_id` it names, so the binding between a tool execution and a slice is a direct stamp and not an inference. The raw session id is never written to disk — the observer stores only a truncated SHA-256 digest of it — and the dispatch record itself never carries a session id, because the dispatch-time producer has no access to one.

No environment variable is required and none is invented: the documented Copilot CLI hook payload is the only authoritative session-id source, and the dispatch record therefore does not need one. The dispatch record is **transient state** in the sense of `R-8`: it holds no date, no clock time, no PII and no payload, and it is **deleted** by the DONE writer when the ledger block is written.

**Ownership of the completion-time measurement.** The DONE writer reads the dispatch record, closes the window, computes the **duration** and the **usage deltas**, writes the ledger block and **deletes** the dispatch record. If the dispatch record is missing, interrupted or corrupt, the writer writes an explicit **`measurement_state: 'UNAVAILABLE'`** ledger with `null` counters and a reason, and the gate refuses a DONE slice that has no ledger at all. The whole path — dispatch record, window, duration, deltas, recovery and cleanup — lives in layer B and never in layer A.

**The gate / writer mechanism that guarantees one ledger per newly completed slice:**

1. **Writer** — `scripts/telemetry/write-slice-ledger.mjs` — deterministic, idempotent upsert into the companion log. It never writes a timestamp, never writes a date, never writes a zero for an unavailable counter.
2. **Gate** — `scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-ledger.gate.mjs` — scans the tracker for slices marked `[DONE]` **at or after the ledger activation marker** and, for each one, requires exactly one valid ledger block in the companion log. A `[DONE]` slice with **no** ledger, a **malformed** ledger, a **duplicate** ledger, or a ledger that contains a forbidden field is a **hard failure**: the DONE transition is refused.
3. **Activation marker** — the ledger requirement is **forward-only**. The gate compares each slice id against the set of slice ids that already carried `[DONE]` before the contract was activated, so the pre-existing DONE slices are never demanded a ledger and are never backfilled. That set is **measured** by the implementation slice (`OT-S3-4`), not assumed from a number quoted in a directive; the directive's "19" is treated as an indication, and the measured set is the authority.
4. **The mirror** — a compact WIP telemetry mirror lives in the **active `.plans.md`** and holds aggregate counters only. It is written by the `07-logging` lane as a tracker edit; **no script ever rewrites the tracker**. The **terminal per-slice DONE ledger lives in the `.logs.md` only**.

**Runtime metadata set (exact):** Node version, duration, validation results, heap usage, RSS usage. Nothing else.

## The persisted-artifact contract (schema v1)

One fenced YAML block per completed slice, in the companion log:

```yaml
telemetry_ledger:
  schema_version: 1
  plan_id: 'opentelemetry-slice-telemetry'
  slice_id: 'OT-S3-2'
  status: '[DONE]'
  measurement_state: 'MEASURED'
  otel_state: 'DISABLED'
  duration_ms: 41233
  runtime:
    node_version: '22.14.0'
    heap_used_bytes: 41234567
    rss_bytes: 98765432
  usage:
    token_usage:
      available: true
      source: 'cortex-get-slice-context'
      measures: 'context tokens DELIVERED to the slice, not model consumption'
      context_tokens_delivered: 18432
      prompt_tokens: null
      completion_tokens: null
      total_tokens: null
      unavailable_reason: 'the repo has no access to the host model accounting'
    tool_executions:
      available: true
      source: 'copilot-cli-posthook-observation-window'
      measures: 'tool EXECUTIONS COMPLETED by the host CLI inside the slice dispatch window - a SUCCESSFUL completion and a FAILED completion are counted as SEPARATELY NAMED measurements; a call DENIED before execution never completes and is NOT observed'
      scope: 'slice-dispatch-window'
      total: 17
      completed_executions: 16
      failed_executions: 1
      sessions_observed: 1
      breakdown:
        read: 9
        edit: 4
        search: 4
        exec: 0
        other: 0
  validation:
    total: 3
    passed: 3
    failed: 0
    skipped: 0
    results:
      - name: 'unit'
        status: 'passed'
        duration_ms: 412
```

The example deliberately shows `otel_state: 'DISABLED'` **together with** `measurement_state: 'MEASURED'` and a real `duration_ms`: the OpenTelemetry layer is off and the repo-owned measurement is still complete. That pairing is the proof that layer A is never required to produce layer B's numbers.

**Contract rules (all pinned by RED tests):**

- **R-1 — Versioned and keyed.** `schema_version` is an integer. The block is keyed by `plan_id` + `slice_id`. A block with a `schema_version` this tracker does not know is reported as `STALE` and repaired, never silently accepted.
- **R-2 — Idempotent rewrite.** Writing the same `(plan_id, slice_id)` twice produces **byte-identical** output. This requires a deterministic emitter (fixed key order, sorted breakdown keys, no timestamps, no random ids, no host-dependent ordering).
- **R-3 — No timestamps, no dates, no clock times, no PII.** The forbidden key set covers `timestamp`, `time`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `timeUnixNano`, `observedTimestamp`, `startedAt`, `completedAt`, `date`, `datetime`, `epoch`, `mtime`, `mtimeMs`, `lastModified`, `lastParsedAt`, `parsedAt`, `writtenAt`, and the forbidden value patterns cover ISO-8601 datetimes, calendar dates, epoch-millisecond literals, absolute Windows paths (a drive letter followed by a path separator), absolute POSIX user paths (a home-directory root, in either the user-home or the system-home form), e-mail addresses and any absolute-path shape. The same scan runs over **every persisted artefact this lane writes**, with **no exclusion**: the layer-A local JSONL, the layer-B tool-execution observation log, the `.logs.md` DONE blocks, the `.plans.md` compact mirror, the **extraction cursor state** and the **derived sidecar index**. A persisted field that would carry an instant is **removed**, never exempted — the `prefixSha256` + size guard already detects a rewrite without a modification time — so the cursor carries **content-derived and offset state only**: `{ source, byteOffset, lineOffset, prefixSha256, sizeAtCursor, blockCount, sliceCount }`, and the observation log carries `{ seq, slice_id, session_key, bucket, outcome }`.
- **R-4 — Explicit availability semantics.** Every usage counter carries `available: true|false`, a `source`, a `measures` string that states **exactly what the counter measures**, and — when `available` is `false` — a `reason` **and `null` numeric fields**. **An unavailable counter is `null`, never `0`.** A zero is a measurement and may only be written when the source actually reported zero.
- **R-5 — No payloads, and every counter is named for what it measures.** No source text, no tool arguments, no tool results, no prompts, no diffs, no file contents. The tool-execution breakdown is a **count per safe bucket** (`read`, `edit`, `search`, `exec`, `other`), never an argument list. A counter that observes only part of the intended universe is **renamed** so that its name states the boundary: the ledger field is `usage.tool_executions` — *tool executions observed by the host CLI hook* — and never `usage.tool_calls`, because the host hook observes completed tool executions and not the number of tool calls the agent issued. **The two completion outcomes are counted and named separately**: `usage.tool_executions.completed_executions` counts the executions the host reported as **successful completions**, `usage.tool_executions.failed_executions` counts the executions the host reported as **failed completions**, and `total` is their sum. A call denied before execution appears in **neither**, because it never completes.
- **R-6 — The compact WIP mirror.** The active `.plans.md` carries aggregate counters only (`slices_completed`, `slices_with_ledger`, `total_duration_ms`, `total_tool_executions`, `total_context_tokens_delivered`, `token_usage_available`, `tool_executions_available`, validation totals). No per-slice rows, no timestamps, no dates.
- **R-7 — Forward-only.** No backfill. The gate demands a ledger only for slices that completed at or after the activation marker.
- **R-8 — Transient state is removed.** The slice's start/end instants exist **only** in the transient dispatch record (`logs/slice-ledger/dispatch/`), are used only to compute the duration delta and the usage window, and are **deleted** when the ledger block is written. The dispatch record carries a **monotonic** counter, never a wall-clock instant, and never a date, a clock time or PII. The only on-disk handoff artifact that survives the slice carries the already-derived `duration_ms` and the aggregate counters. A RED test asserts that the dispatch record for a completed slice no longer exists. **The deletion is performed by the layer-B DONE writer** (`scripts/telemetry/write-slice-ledger.mjs`): no layer-A module creates, reads, measures or deletes a layer-B transient artefact, and layer A never computes a duration.

## The token and tool-execution attribution contract

**The measured answer, stated honestly, in three parts.**

1. **There is NO per-slice LLM token-consumption source in this repository today, and none is coming.** The repo has no access to the host agent's model accounting. The ledger records `available: false` with a reason and `null` counters and never writes `0`. This part is unchanged by this patch.
2. **There is NO per-slice tool-call counter in this repository today.** That finding was correct and is still correct — `NEATAPTIC_SLICE_ID` has **zero** references repo-wide, the per-session carrier `rag-index/data/hook-context/hook-context-<sessionId>.json` carries `planPath`, `activePhase`, `activeStep` and `currentAgent` but **no slice id** (`scripts/agent-customization/enforcement/runtime-enforcement.mjs:88-98` carrier path, `:118-130` carrier shape, `:176-185` the `preparedAction` fields), and the enforcement CLI accepts `--plan`, `--phase` and `--step` only (`scripts/agent-customization/enforcement/runtime-enforcement-context.mjs:108-113`). **What the earlier draft got wrong was the remedy**: it promised a "slice-scoped usage hook" that resolves the slice id from an environment variable that nothing sets, and it named no owner for the file that would have to bind a session to a slice. This patch replaces that promise with an owned, executable and honestly-scoped boundary — see *The ratified instrumentation contract* below.
3. **The host CLI does report every completed tool execution to a repo-owned hook, and this repo already registers one.** The authoritative Copilot CLI hook reference documents `preToolUse`, `postToolUse` and `postToolUseFailure` events whose payloads carry the session id and the tool name. The two post events are **separate event keys**: `postToolUse` fires "after each tool completes **successfully**" and `postToolUseFailure` fires "after a tool completes with a **failure**" — and a failing tool call **skips `postToolUse` entirely**, so a failure is observable only through the failure key. The reference also states that a `matcher` is an **optional regex compiled as `^(?:PATTERN)$` and tested against the whole tool name**, that **an invalid regular expression causes the hook entry to be skipped** (with a `! Invalid hook configuration in FILE: REASON` diagnostic), and that the correct way to receive every tool is to **omit `matcher`**. The "`*`, `**` or an empty matcher fires for every tool" rule is scoped to the PascalCase `PreToolUse` (Claude-format) matchers and does **not** apply to `postToolUse`, so a bare `*` is **not** a valid pattern there. The repo's own `.github/hooks/cortex-refresh.json` already registers a `PostToolUse` hook, and the repo's existing hook code already reads the host payload's tool-name and session-id fields. So the missing piece was never the host surface — it was the **repo-owned binding, the ownership, the correct registration of BOTH post events, and the honest naming of the counter**. That is what this patch adds.

### The measured evidence (T1 → AC-011, AC-012, AC-013)

| signal | what exists today | measured site | availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **duration** | a monotonic elapsed measurement | `src/neat/evolve/runtime/evolve.runtime.utils.ts:152-158`, `:211-218` (`resolveHighResolutionNow()`); the injectable-clock precedent at `examples/neatRacing/ai/runtime.adaptation.ts:263,301,376,710`; the fail-open wrapper precedent at `src/neat/telemetry/runtime/telemetry.runtime.ts:73-93` | **available now**, but **owned by layer B**: it is produced by the repo-owned DONE path, never by the OpenTelemetry layer (`AC-012`) |
| **RAG context tokens** | a per-slice context-size estimate | `scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-workflow-mcp.mjs:1167` (`get_slice_context` → `token_count`), accumulated at `:884-885` and defaulted at `:622`; the estimator is `rag-index/assemble-context.mjs:28` (`DEFAULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4`), `:177-179`, `:559`; the budget plumbing is `scripts/mcp-semantic/tools/search-context.mjs:403,410,411,412,422` and `:65,148-151` | **available now**, but it measures **context tokens DELIVERED**, **not** model consumption — the field is named `context_tokens_delivered` for exactly that reason. It also **had no owner**: the count lived only in the MCP response and nothing persisted it. This patch gives it one — the dispatch-time producer that opens the slice window persists it (`AC-011`) |
| **per-call token counters** | per-call, not per-slice | `scripts/mcp-semantic/tools/search-context.mjs:403` (`token_count`), `:410` (`tokens_used`), `:411` (`context_budget_consumed`), `:422` (`metadata.totalTokens`); `search-advanced.mjs:303,949` | per-call only; not attributable to a slice |
| **LLM prompt / completion tokens** | **nothing** | — | **NOT available.** The repo has no access to the host agent's model accounting. The ledger records `available: false` with a reason and `null` counters. |
| **tool calls, per agent session** | a runtime-only field that is never persisted | `.github/copilot-instructions.md:217`; `.github/skills/execute/SKILL.md:569,629,644,908`; `.github/skills/routing-optimization-policy/SKILL.md:296` — **6 documentation lines**; **0 references** under `src/`, `scripts/` or `testing/` (the only other occurrences are the generated `semantic-snapshot.json` artifacts under `docs/assets/` and `rag-index/snapshots/`) | **NOT persistable** from repo code |
| **write-tool calls, per session** | the closest real counter | `scripts/agent-customization/hooks/post-write-reindex-hook.mjs:44` (`WRITE_TOOL_PATTERN`, write tools only), `:55` (early return for every other tool), `:133`/`:137` (one line per triggering call), `:152` (the append writer, which logs `new Date().toISOString()`); registered as `PostToolUse` in `.github/hooks/cortex-refresh.json` | **not a telemetry source and never ingested**: it matches write tools only, carries no slice id, and every line carries a **timestamp** and a **file path**. It is evidence that the repo's hook surface receives the host payload; it is **not** the counter |
| **the host tool-execution surface** | the host CLI reports **every** completed tool execution to a repo-owned hook | the authoritative reference is the Copilot CLI `hooks-reference` page (`docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference`): the `postToolUse` event (fired after each tool completes **successfully**) and the `postToolUseFailure` event (fired after a tool completes with a **failure**) are **two separate event keys**, and both carry the session id, the tool name and the working directory; a failing call **skips `postToolUse` entirely** and is observable only through the failure key. The reference states that a `matcher` is an **optional regex compiled as `^(?:PATTERN)$` and tested against the tool name**, that an **invalid** pattern causes the **hook entry to be skipped** with a `! Invalid hook configuration in FILE: REASON` diagnostic, and that the correct way to receive every tool is to **omit `matcher`** — the "`*` fires for every tool" rule belongs to the PascalCase `PreToolUse` matchers only. The host maps its runtime tools onto the Claude-compatible names `Bash`, `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `AskUserQuestion`, `TodoWrite`, `Agent`. The repo corroborates the payload shape with its own code: `scripts/agent-customization/hooks/post-write-reindex-hook.mjs` reads the payload's tool-name field, and `scripts/agent-customization/enforcement/runtime-enforcement.mjs:26-42` (`resolveSessionId`) reads `input.session_id` / `input.sessionId` | **available to a repo-owned hook.** This is the evidenced boundary the counter is built on |
| **the session id as an environment variable** | **no documented source** | the documented Copilot CLI environment variables are `GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_AGENT_PROMPT`, `HOME`, `COPILOT_HOME`, `COPILOT_PLUGIN_DATA`, `COPILOT_HOOK_ALLOW_LOCALHOST` — **none of them is a session id**. The repo's `COPILOT_SESSION_ID` / `GITHUB_COPILOT_SESSION_ID` / `COPILOT_CLI_SESSION_ID` fallbacks at `scripts/agent-customization/enforcement/runtime-enforcement.mjs:30-32` are **repo-invented**, not documented | **NOT available.** The design therefore never requires an environment variable to carry the session id or the slice id |
| **gate and convergence counters** | per-slice, but not usage | `slice-advancement` `gateCount` / `specialistCount`; `convergence-tracker` `iterationCount` | per-slice but the wrong quantity |

`.github/ai-learning/learning-log.jsonl` is an **append-only** log, so its absolute line count drifts and is **not** quoted as a constant. The load-bearing finding is structural and was re-measured on the current bytes: a `slice_id` key appears on only a small minority of its lines (**29** on the current bytes), and **no** line carries a token-usage or tool-usage field — every occurrence of the words `token` or `tool` in that file is prose inside a learning-event description, never a usage field. The implementation slice re-measures both facts with the same rules instead of relying on an absolute line total.

### The ratified instrumentation contract (owned end to end)

**Precondition — an executable probe, not a document.** The contract below is **not** asserted by prose. `OT-S1-3` is an **executable probe slice**: `scripts/telemetry/probe-attribution-sources.mjs` runs against the live repository, persists a machine-readable report, and its focused test asserts that every `file:line` the report cites resolves to a real file and a real line, and that the research artifact `plans/opentelemetry-slice-telemetry.research.md` agrees with the probe output. The dependent implementation slices are **blocked until the probe has demonstrated each source** (or recorded it as unavailable, with the reason). If the probe cannot demonstrate a source, the dependent slice writes `available: false` with the probe's reason — it does not fabricate a number. `AC-013`.

1. **Tool executions — a new repo-owned observer, honestly scoped.**
   - **Owner:** `scripts/agent-customization/hooks/slice-usage-hook.mjs` (implemented by `OT-S6-2`), registered in `.github/hooks/cortex-refresh.json` as **two** entries beside the existing write-reindex hook: one under the **success** event key `PostToolUse` and one under the **failure** event key `PostToolUseFailure`, both running the **same** command. The failure entry is **not optional**: a failing tool call skips `postToolUse` entirely, so an observer registered under the success key alone would never see a failure and the persisted `measures` string would then over-claim.
   - **What it observes:** every tool execution the host CLI reports as **completed** — `postToolUse` (a successful completion) and `postToolUseFailure` (a failed completion) — for **all** tools, not only the write tools. The two outcomes are counted and named **separately**: `completed_executions` and `failed_executions`.
   - **The matcher rule, as the authoritative reference states it:** a `matcher` is **optional**; it is a regex compiled as `^(?:PATTERN)$` and tested against the **whole** tool name; an **invalid** regex causes the **hook entry to be skipped** (the CLI prints `! Invalid hook configuration in FILE: REASON`); and the correct way to receive every tool is to **omit `matcher`**. The "`*` fires for every tool" rule is scoped to the PascalCase `PreToolUse` matchers and does **not** apply to `postToolUse`. **Both observer entries therefore carry NO `matcher` field at all**, and the failure key takes **no** matcher field either (it is not a matcher-matched event). A RED test asserts that no observer entry carries a `matcher` and that every matcher present anywhere in the manifest compiles under `^(?:PATTERN)$`, so the observer can never be silently skipped by an invalid pattern.
   - **The payload handling, for both events and both spellings:** the observer accepts the camelCase payload (`sessionId`, `toolName`, `toolArgs`, `toolResult`, `error`) and the VS Code payload (`session_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_result`, `error`) — the same tolerance the repo's existing hook already applies (`hookInput.tool_name ?? hookInput.toolName`). The success payload carries `toolResult` and the failure payload carries `error`; the observer reads the **tool name** (to derive the safe bucket) and the **session id** (to derive the truncated digest) and **uses nothing else**. It persists **no** hook `timestamp`, **no** `cwd`, **no** `toolArgs`, **no** `toolResult`, **no** error text, **no** tool name, **no** content, **no** path and **no** raw session id — the failure path is therefore **no less private** than the success path.
   - **The hook-load boundary:** repository hooks are loaded by the CLI at **startup** or after a **`/cd`** into the repository, so a manifest change is **not** live in the session that wrote it. The end-to-end proof (`OT-S6-3`) therefore has to run in a **fresh session** (or after the documented reload boundary) and must **prove that the observer actually fired**; a proof taken in the writing session would measure an observer that was never loaded. `AC-011-E`.
   - **What it writes:** one **append-only** line per execution to `logs/slice-ledger/tool-executions.jsonl`, carrying exactly five fields: `seq` (the observation line's **append-time line index** in that log — the derivation and the concurrency protocol are specified below), `slice_id` (stamped from the open dispatch record), `session_key` (a truncated SHA-256 of the host session id — the raw id is never written), `bucket` (`read` | `edit` | `search` | `exec` | `other`, derived **in memory** from the host tool name, which is never written) and `outcome` (`completed` | `failed`). It writes **no** tool name, **no** argument, **no** result, **no** error content, **no** content, **no** path, **no** timestamp, **no** date and **no** raw session id. When no dispatch record is open the observer writes **nothing** — the observation log holds only slice-attributable lines.
   - **The sequence derivation and the write protocol — specified, not asserted:** the observation log is opened in **append** mode (`O_APPEND`) and each observation is written as **exactly one** `write()` of **exactly one** complete line, so a concurrent append cannot interleave inside a line. `seq` is that line's **append-time line index** — it is **derived from the log's own line order**, not from a global counter file. Two concurrent sessions may therefore produce the **same** `seq` value for two different lines, and the DONE writer **tolerates** that: it counts the **lines** whose `seq` is **greater than the dispatch sequence** and never counts **distinct** `seq` values, so a duplicate `seq` cannot inflate the total. A line that does not parse is **quarantined** to a `.bak` sibling through the same quarantine mechanism the corrupt path uses, and the tool-execution counter is then reported `available: false` with a reason — the ledger stays honestly writable, so this is **not** a layer-B `CORRUPT` state and does **not** refuse the DONE transition. The write is retried a **bounded** number of times on a transient I/O error, and the observer is **fail-open**: a failed observation never fails the tool call it observed.
   - **How the slice id is bound — the session → slice binding:** the hook resolves the slice id by reading the **open dispatch record** that the dispatch-time producer wrote, and it **stamps** that `slice_id` onto the execution. The binding is therefore a **direct stamp**, not an inference from a guessed id: the host payload carries no slice id and no documented environment variable carries one, so the repo owns the binding at dispatch time. The DONE writer closes the window: it counts the stamped lines whose `seq` is greater than the dispatch sequence, and deletes the dispatch record.
   - **The honest boundary, stated in full.** *Counted:* every tool execution the host CLI reports as completed while the slice's dispatch record is open, across all tools — the successful completions as `completed_executions` and the failed completions as `failed_executions`, so a reader sees the failure count without inferring it. *Not counted:* a tool call **denied** by a `preToolUse` hook (it never completes, so neither post event fires), and any tool execution outside the open window. *Not claimed:* the number of tool calls the agent **issued**, and a per-session attribution beyond the stamp. The one residual ambiguity is stated rather than hidden: the observer cannot tell **which** session opened the dispatch record, so an execution from a different session that lands while the slice is open is stamped with that slice id. The ledger therefore reports `sessions_observed` and the per-session breakdown, so any concurrent session is **visible**, never silently folded in. The ledger field is named `usage.tool_executions` and never `usage.tool_calls`, and it carries `measures` and `scope` so that no reader can mistake it for a wider quantity.
   - **Enforcement at the DONE boundary:** the DONE writer **must** produce a usage snapshot; the DONE gate **refuses** a ledger whose tool-execution counter claims `available: true` without a `source`, a `measures` string and a `scope`, and **refuses** a ledger in which an unavailable counter was written as `0`.
2. **Tokens — the existing per-slice context count, now persisted by an owner.**
   - **Owner:** the same dispatch-time producer inside `scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-workflow-mcp.mjs` (implemented by `OT-S1-4`). `get_slice_context` already computes the per-slice `token_count` at `:884-885` and returns it at `:1167`; that value was previously **discarded** because nothing persisted it. The producer now writes it into the slice's transient dispatch record together with the window start, and the DONE writer copies it into the ledger as `context_tokens_delivered` with `source: 'cortex-get-slice-context'` and the `measures` string "context tokens DELIVERED to the slice, not model consumption".
   - **The distinction is enforced, not merely named:** `context_tokens_delivered` (the size of the context the repo served to the slice) and `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens` / `total_tokens` (the host model's consumption) are **separate fields**. The three model-consumption fields stay `null` with an `unavailable_reason` until a host accounting surface exists. `AC-011`.
3. **Duration, the window and the transient state — owned by the fail-closed layer.** The dispatch record (slice identity, window start, delivered-context-token count, the monotonic base) is written by the dispatch-time producer and closed by the DONE writer; the writer computes `duration_ms`, computes the usage deltas, writes the ledger and **deletes** the dispatch record. The OpenTelemetry layer is never in that path. A missing, interrupted or corrupt dispatch record yields `measurement_state: 'UNAVAILABLE'` with `null` counters and a reason — never `0` — and a missing ledger still fails the gate closed. `AC-012`.
4. **LLM prompt / completion tokens — reported as unavailable.** They are `available: false` with a reason string. If the host later exposes a persistable per-slice accounting field, the contract gains a fourth counter; until then the ledger says "unavailable" and never `0`.
5. **What the probe must demonstrate before any dependent slice runs.** The probe report must name, with a resolving `file:line`: (a) the host hook events and payload fields the observer depends on, corroborated by the repo's own hook code; (b) the absence of any documented session-id environment variable; (c) the per-slice `token_count` computation site and the **absence** of any persistence of it before this contract; (d) the absence of any per-slice LLM token-consumption source; (e) the existence and the exact limits of the write-tool hook. A dependent slice that cannot find its source in the report writes `available: false` with the report's reason.
